James Madison Dukes.previous_hc_experience: Extensive, and the Coaching Carousel weighs both halves of it: Billy Napier's stint in Gainesville was an abject disaster, but he was really good at Louisiana, winning 40 games in four seasons. It adds that he inherited a solid foundation from Mark Hudspeth there and gets the same here.
James Madison Dukes.oc: Cam Aiken, whom the guide calls a rising star.
James Madison Dukes.dc: Robert Bala, who has worked under Napier, Jedd Fisch — with coordinator Stephen Belichick — and Nick Saban over the past three years.
James Madison Dukes.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
James Madison Dukes.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
James Madison Dukes.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
James Madison Dukes.offensive_scheme: Not named, but characterised by the coordinator's record: a Clemson graduate on staff for two National Championships, time under Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss, then his own offense at East Tennessee State where the Buccaneers scored over 32 points per game with better than 440 yards per game, plus running backs at South Florida in a group that ran for nearly 200 yards per game in 2022. The guide expects him to keep the throttle down on an offense that averaged 6.4 yards per play and 37.1 points per game.
James Madison Dukes.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide lays out four FBS seasons of consistency: 2.5, 2.6, 3.5 and 2.8 yards per carry allowed, with 4.7, 5.0, 4.9 and 4.4 yards per play.
James Madison Dukes.tempo: Not addressed directly. The guide's phrase is keeping the throttle down.
James Madison Dukes.run_pass: Expected to lean on the run early: the guide argues a run-heavy approach could keep pressure off a first-time starter, with a returning back plus a transfer who averaged over seven yards per carry at Drake, behind an offensive line suited to running the ball.
James Madison Dukes.qb_development: The central question the guide puts to the new staff, and it records a deliberate institutional choice behind it: with NIL funds allocated elsewhere, the Dukes essentially did not take the portal route at quarterback, placing faith in JC Evans, a 6-foot-5 sophomore who was not a highly sought recruit but spent two years learning behind Alonza Barnett. It adds a coaching data point — Michigan State was not great last season, but its quarterbacks posted a 20-to-6 touchdown-to-interception ratio, and pass game coordinator Aaron Pflugrad is the Dukes' new quarterbacks coach.
James Madison Dukes.continuity: None. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator, 0 for the quarterback and 0 for 5 returning starters — a total of 0.
James Madison Dukes.staff_turnover: Complete, and the guide stresses why it matters here: a promising coaching staff matters hugely given the volume of transfers. It also notes the programme has absorbed staff changes without downturn before, during the Cignetti-to-Chesney transition.
James Madison Dukes.prior_school: Louisiana and Florida for Napier; Clemson, Ole Miss, East Tennessee State and South Florida for Cam Aiken; and Napier's, Jedd Fisch's and Nick Saban's staffs for Robert Bala. On the roster the guide records Nick Herman from Drake and Davi Belfort from UCF.
James Madison Dukes.portal_recruiting: The programme's defining competence, and its current risk. The guide's headline claim is that no Sun Belt team has leveraged the transfer portal better than James Madison, crediting resources plus masterful talent identification by Curt Cignetti and Bob Chesney, especially at quarterback, and naming Jordan McCloud and Alonza Barnett as having upheld the standards through the FCS-to-FBS transition. 247Sports graded this year's haul best in the conference by a wide margin — which the guide calls fortunate, since nearly all of last season's production is gone — while cautioning that many additions come from lower divisions, FCS, or Power Four programmes where they never saw the field.
James Madison Dukes.vsin_assessment: A hard act to follow, with the risk located in the roster rather than the man. The Coaching Carousel says following up Cignetti and Chesney was going to be an unenviable task for anybody, calls the Florida stint an abject disaster while crediting 40 wins in four seasons at Louisiana, notes Florida is a different beast and some men just aren't built for that burden, and concludes that if JMU struggles it'll likely be less about Napier and more about the mass exodus of talent over the last two seasons. The team pages call Cam Aiken an outstanding hire, are explicit about their own asymmetry — bullish on the offense, not sure they can be on the defense — and offer a precedent: the season after Cignetti left, the Dukes went 9-4 but only 4-4 in conference play.
James Madison Dukes.strengths: A head coach with 40 wins in four seasons at his last Sun Belt job, an offensive coordinator the guide calls a rising star and an outstanding hire, a defensive coordinator schooled under Napier, Jedd Fisch and Nick Saban, the best-graded portal haul in the conference by a wide margin, and a defense with four straight seasons of consistency to build on.
James Madison Dukes.concerns: A Stability Score of 0 with five returning starters and nearly all production gone, a quarterback deliberately not upgraded through the portal, portal additions drawn largely from lower divisions or players who never saw the field at Power Four programmes, and roster attrition the guide says has to bite the defense eventually.
James Madison Dukes.betting: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins. The precedent it leans on is Bob Chesney's first regular season producing 8-4, which it could see repeated, with the quarterback position a major question mark.
James Madison Dukes.carousel_summary: Adam Burke frames the job first: following up Curt Cignetti and Bob Chesney was going to be an unenviable task for anybody, but it's 'Sun Belt Billy' who gets the chance. He does not soften the recent record — his stint in Gainesville was an abject disaster — but immediately balances it: he was really good at Louisiana, winning 40 games in four seasons, and he inherited a solid foundation from Mark Hudspeth there and gets the same here with the Dukes. His explanation is about fit rather than ability: Florida is a different beast and some guys just aren't built for that burden. His conclusion assigns the risk elsewhere — if JMU struggles, it'll likely be less about Napier and more about the mass exodus of talent over the last two seasons.

Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed as prior head-coaching experience. The guide records Michael Desormeaux as the former offensive coordinator under Billy Napier, a Ragin' Cajun quarterback from 2005-08, and the man who coached the bowl at the end of Napier's tenure.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.dc: Jim Salgado, entering his second year.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.offensive_scheme: Not named, but the identity is stated clearly: this is a big offensive line group and the plan is plainly to run the ball as much as possible, supported by the fact that Louisiana had only one game with 30 pass attempts in conference play last season.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide locates the concern in the pass rush: 23 sacks in 13 games and a tie for 112th in tackles for loss per game.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.run_pass: Heavily run-weighted, both by design and by personnel, with the health of the run-blockers described as paramount.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide's assessment of Lunch Winfield is split by skill — a mediocre-at-best passer with an 11-to-7 ratio and 58.8% completions, but a genuine runner with 667 yards and nine rushing touchdowns — and it suggests the clarity of him having the job outright may help, since Tim Leger can now scheme the offense exclusively around him.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.continuity: Complete. The Stability Score table (p. 43) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 2 for 10 returning starters — totalling 16.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.prior_school: Louisiana itself, where Desormeaux played and coached under Napier.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.portal_recruiting: Identified as the guide's central worry. It records the fewest portal additions in the conference and offers two possible explanations: either there is not much money there, or nobody is willing to invest it. Its worry is stated as the complete lack of portal involvement while other conference programmes improve externally and Louisiana relies on internal development. It also calls it surprising that the staff did not attack the portal more aggressively for offensive line depth.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.vsin_assessment: A tenure measured against its immediate predecessor and found wanting. The guide says this season feels really, really big for Desormeaux, allows that having been a Ragin' Cajun quarterback probably buys him some leeway, then sets the record against it: three 6-7 seasons plus one 10-4 that ended in a 31-3 conference title game loss and a 34-3 bowl loss. It adds a pointed detail about his own specialism — the former offensive coordinator saw his offense fall by 4.9 points and 1.3 yards per play year over year — and draws the Napier comparison in arithmetic: Desormeaux has 28 wins in four seasons, while Napier had seven losses in year one and only five in total after that. It states plainly that it does not know that things are working, and notes he received a five-year extension after the 10-4 season and then reverted right back to his prior form.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.strengths: A Stability Score of 16 with head coach, both coordinators and the quarterback all returning; programme roots that the guide says buy the coach leeway; a settled quarterback the offense can now be built around exclusively; a big offensive line with a clear identity; and injury-forced experience gained by depth linemen.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.concerns: Three 6-7 seasons in four, an offense that declined by 4.9 points and 1.3 yards per play under an offensive-minded head coach, the fewest portal additions in the conference, a pass rush of 23 sacks in 13 games, and top tacklers gone after 220 combined stops.
Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns.betting: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins. The guide's reasoning is explicitly about the coach and the programme's roster strategy: it does not know that things are working with Desormeaux, the athletic department may face a big decision, and the complete lack of portal involvement leaves Louisiana relying on internal development while rivals improve externally. It also notes how narrow last season's bowl run was — three of the four closing wins came by four points or fewer, as did four of the five conference wins.

Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.dc: Luke Olsen, who was in his first year in the role last season.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.

Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide complicates the picture of last year's unit — under Olsen the Bulldogs allowed marginally fewer points per game, 20.8 against 21, while giving up 0.6 more yards per carry, 67 more passing yards per game and 0.7 more yards per play.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated philosophy, but the guide shows how concentrated the rushing production was: four games accounted for 1,486 of 2,540 rushing yards, leaving just 1,054 across the other nine.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records the quarterbacks collectively posting an 8-to-9 touchdown-to-interception ratio and argues things could have gone very differently without Trey Kukuk's running — he threw more interceptions than touchdowns but averaged better than six yards per carry.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.continuity: Head coach, defensive coordinator and quarterback return; the offensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 3 and 4, plus 1 for 9 returning starters, totalling 12.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive coordinator per the Stability Score table. The guide notes the defense was very strong for a second straight season even through a coordinator change.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.portal_recruiting: Not addressed as a staff-driven effect.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.vsin_assessment: A breakthrough season the guide reads as fragile, arriving at the wrong moment. It puts last year in career context — 11 wins across the first three seasons combined before everything came together — and reads the improvement as the offense finally carrying its weight to support a defense that was strong for a second straight season. Its conclusion is one of timing: with notable personnel losses and signs of defensive regression, this might be a bad moment to switch conferences. It calls the defense very ripe for regression and says the abundance of closely lined games makes that a prominent factor in its handicapping.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.strengths: A defense that held up through a coordinator change for a second straight strong season, defensive-coordinator continuity in year two, a returning quarterback, and a head coach coming off his best season.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.concerns: An entirely new secondary with one of Conference USA's best players gone plus two defensive backs who combined for 17 pass breakups, the three leading tacklers all departed, underlying defensive metrics that worsened even as points allowed held, rushing production concentrated in four games, and a step up in conference strength.
Louisiana Tech Bulldogs.betting: The guide's projection is 5.76 wins, above the number, but it calls the defense very ripe for regression and notes Louisiana Tech is favoured by more than two points only three times — against Northwestern State, UL Monroe and Southern Miss — making that regression a prominent factor in its handicapping. It also measures the conference step-up two ways and concludes the average fan and bettor will not think much of the difference.

Marshall Thundering Herd.previous_hc_experience: None before this. The guide records that Tony Gibson was a coordinator for a decade at West Virginia and NC State before this first head job.
Marshall Thundering Herd.dc: Brad Lambert, the former Charlotte head coach, back for a third stint at Marshall after coaching this defense in 2019-20 and starting with the programme in the early 1990s.
Marshall Thundering Herd.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Marshall Thundering Herd.dc_status: New — the guide records Lambert's return, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Marshall Thundering Herd.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Marshall Thundering Herd.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Marshall Thundering Herd.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide quantifies the collapse it must fix: with the offense broadly unchanged, the defense allowed 7.2 more points and 0.6 more yards per play, including an increase of more than 60 passing yards per game.
Marshall Thundering Herd.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Marshall Thundering Herd.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Carlos Del Rio-Wilson finding a home after bouncing around through Florida and Syracuse, leading the team in rushing with 661 yards while throwing for more than 2,000 and accounting for 23 total touchdowns in his first crack as a starter.
Marshall Thundering Herd.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 1 for 9 returning starters, totalling 12.
Marshall Thundering Herd.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive coordinator, and the guide's reasoning about the hire is explicitly about familiarity: Lambert has been around a long time, this defense badly needs help, and going to an old friend makes sense.
Marshall Thundering Herd.prior_school: Marshall itself for Lambert across three stints, plus Charlotte, Wake Forest and Kentucky. West Virginia and NC State are Gibson's coordinator background. The guide also notes Coastal Carolina is now coached by Ryan Beard, who put 474 yards on the Herd last season when he was at Missouri State.
Marshall Thundering Herd.portal_recruiting: Rated weak in aggregate and targeted in detail. The guide records that a 5-7 team did not really improve through the portal or the freshman class, judged by conference ranking, while noting receiver was a focal point and cornerback a major portal focus after Marshall allowed 262 passing yards per game.
Marshall Thundering Herd.vsin_assessment: Two readings of the season, and a test set for the coach. The guide's first reading is that the athletic department got what it deserved for letting Charles Huff walk after he won the Sun Belt at 10-3, and its judgement on the coach follows: in a rebuilding year Gibson did a pretty good job to get the team as far as he did, even with a disappointing ending. It grants the mitigating context in full — a massive rebuilding job simply to field enough capable bodies, with the programme down to just over 40 players after the mass departures in December and January — then states plainly that those excuses are now spent if Gibson again fails as a favourite or cannot close out games. Its evidence is that his team lost five games as a favourite, missed a bowl despite a +6 turnover margin, and lost two games in which it out-gained the opponent by 275 and 156 yards.
Marshall Thundering Herd.strengths: A returning quarterback who accounted for 23 total touchdowns and led the team in rushing, offensive-coordinator continuity, an offense that held its level through a rebuilding year, a defensive coordinator with three prior stints at the programme, a conference-best-rated tight end, and receiver addressed as a portal focal point.
Marshall Thundering Herd.concerns: A first-time head coach who lost five games as a favourite, a defense that gave up 7.2 more points per game and over 60 more passing yards, three 5-plus-yards-per-carry backs and the leading receiver gone, and a portal and freshman class that did not improve the roster by conference ranking.
Marshall Thundering Herd.betting: The guide's coaching-linked market observation is the favourite-role record: five losses as a favourite in year one, with excuses now spent. It adds a specific warning that Coastal Carolina is now coached by Ryan Beard, who put 474 yards on the Herd last season, and lands on a tough slate with a projection of 7.35 wins.

Old Dominion Monarchs.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide describes Ricky Rahne as an offensive-minded coach whose programme improved by five wins to finish 10-3.
Old Dominion Monarchs.oc: Kody Cook, promoted from wide receivers coach, who also takes the quarterbacks. Kevin Decker left for the same role at Memphis.
Old Dominion Monarchs.oc_status: New — the guide records Decker's departure and Cook's promotion, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Old Dominion Monarchs.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Old Dominion Monarchs.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Old Dominion Monarchs.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide expects a run-heavy team again.
Old Dominion Monarchs.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide tracks Seiler's pass rush across three years — 19 sacks, then 26, then 39 — alongside a top-25 third-down defense, and records the unit cutting 9.5 points and 0.9 yards per play to hold opponents to 18.5 points and 4.8 yards per play.
Old Dominion Monarchs.run_pass: Run-weighted and expected to remain so, with Devin Roche at 5.7 yards per carry and JUCO transfer Trey Hall named as the backfield.
Old Dominion Monarchs.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide weighs continuity against upside — Quinn Henicle is the holdover who knows the system but was not very good at 42.5% completions, while Jaxon Potter was the higher-graded recruit — and keeps both the doubt and the urgency: neither looks poised to top Colton Joseph's numbers, and Rahne needs to get this right and fix it early in the season.
Old Dominion Monarchs.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 0 for 7 returning starters, totalling 7.
Old Dominion Monarchs.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive side but with knock-on shifts: Kevin Decker left for Memphis, Kody Cook was promoted from wide receivers and also took the quarterbacks, with other shifts across the staff. The guide calls Cook — who played at Kansas State and coached at Tennessee — the logical promotion.
Old Dominion Monarchs.prior_school: Memphis is where Decker went. Kansas State and Tennessee are Cook's background. On the roster the guide records Trey Hall as a JUCO transfer originally an Ole Miss commit.
Old Dominion Monarchs.portal_recruiting: Addressed through the losses rather than the gains. The guide generalises this into a structural observation about the Group of Six era: whiplash seasons are very possible now because of the portal, with some teams completely wrecked and others staying intact enough to take advantage — and places ODU on the wrong side of that this year.
Old Dominion Monarchs.vsin_assessment: A ten-win season the guide credits substantially to one coordinator, arriving before heavy losses. It first credits Rahne, an offensive-minded coach, with finally rounding the defense into form — up in yards per carry and points per game in each of the last three seasons — before arguing the real separator was Blake Seiler's defense. On this season it records very heavy losses headlined by the quarterback to Wisconsin and the offensive coordinator to Memphis, and its calibrated verdict on the defense is to buy them as better than 2024 but worse than 2025.
Old Dominion Monarchs.strengths: A defensive coordinator with a three-year pass-rush progression from 19 to 39 sacks and a top-25 third-down defense, defensive-coordinator continuity, returning starters at each level plus two linebackers back from injury, and an internal promotion the guide calls logical.
Old Dominion Monarchs.concerns: Only seven returning starters, the loss of a quarterback who rushed for more than 1,000 yards and threw for over 2,600, the loss of the offensive coordinator to Memphis, all three of the team's 11-plus-catch receivers gone with nobody else exceeding 200 yards, and two quarterback candidates the guide says are unlikely to match the departed starter.
Old Dominion Monarchs.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching.
